newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Sluggish trade on Morocco's stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish trade on Morocco's stock exchange.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.04 percent lower with ONA group falling for a second consecutive day and low volumes traded in most stocks, stockbrokers said.
Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 639.18 points from 639.45 points on Tuesday.
"Overall the market is very cautious, most stocks had very low volumes traded except for Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur," a broker at Casablanca-based Sogebourse said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, fell 10 dirhams to 760 dirhams.
Second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in May 1996, dropped 27 dirhams to 1,140 dirhams with 979 bonds traded.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's second largest capitalisation, was down one dirham to 860 dirhams with 683 shares exchanged.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir edged down one dirham to 340 dirhams with 570 shares traded.

Among others gaining were BMCE, up six dirhams to 611 dirhams, accounting for the main trade on the official market with more than 20,000 shares changing hands. Steel giant Sonasid rose 11 dirhams to 550 dirhams and Societe Nationale d'Investissement edged up two dirhams to 720 dirhams.

Privatisation Minister Abderrahmane Saadi said on Wednesday that the sale of 20 percent of Imiter silver mine was 5.87 times oversubscribed. Up to 329,018 shares were on offer at 396 dirhams per share from June 9-13.
Total traded volume on the official market was 38.3 million dirhams from 39.7 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 10.4 million from 25.3 million dirhams.
